text:
Predicates:
Mammal(x) ::: x is a mammal.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Monkey(x) ::: x is a monkey.
Bird(x) ::: x is a bird.
Fly(x) ::: x can fly.
HasWings(x) ::: x has wings.
Breathes(x) ::: x breathes.
Rock ::: Rock is a specific individual.

Premises:
∀x (Mammal(x) → Animal(x)) ::: All mammals are animals.
∀x (Monkey(x) → Mammal(x)) ::: All monkeys are mammals.
Animal(x) → (Monkey(x) ∨ Bird(x)) ::: An animal is either a monkey or a bird.
∀x (Bird(x) → Fly(x)) ::: All birds fly.
∀x (Animal(x) → Breathes(x)) ::: All animals breathe.
∀x (Fly(x) → HasWings(x)) ::: If something can fly, then it has wings.
¬(Fly(Rock)) ∧ ¬(Bird(Rock)) → ¬(Fly(Rock)) ∧ ¬(Breathes(Rock)) ::: If Rock is neither a fly nor a bird, then Rock neither flies nor breathes.

Conclusion:
Rock is a monkey ::: Monkey(Rock)
